Subject: Tenant handback: certification & rollback scenarios

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this call earlier. Lumina is starting to draft the exit commitments for our private VPC deployment and we need a concrete picture of two things before legal can finalise the contract amendment:

1) The attestation artifacts you provide when a tenant requests a handback / deletion (timeline, proof-of-delete, manifest).
2) If we or a regulator later need to rehydrate data for a limited audit window, what rollback or short-term restore options exist, and under what explicit conditions.

A few specifics from our side:
- Our security team wants to know whether you provide a signed deletion manifest (hashes + timestamps) and whether Redwood can provide a third-party notarized statement.
- We use a customer-managed S3 endpoint for snapshot exports. Are exports under customer control or Redwood-managed?
- Can you provide a typical timeline (business days) for: snapshot creation, manifest issuance, deletion (tombstone + overwrite), and final verification?

If you could attach a checklist or example artifacts, that would help speed legal review. Attaching the original statement of work for context.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Director, IT Security
Lumina Diagnostics

Subject: Re: Tenant handback: certification & rollback scenarios

Alex — thanks for the clear list. I’ll outline the standard Redwood handback package and call out where we can make contract-level commitments versus operational options. Quick summary up-front, then attachments below.

Quick answers (summary):
- Artifacts: Yes — we provide a signed deletion manifest (SHA256 of snapshot blobs, generation timestamps, storage locations) and a machine-signed deletion certificate. For customers that require it we offer an independently notarized attestation (third-party notary) as an add-on.
- Snapshot ownership: By default, snapshot exports are customer-owned when you configure a customer-managed export bucket (we support both customer-managed and Redwood-managed export flows). If you choose customer-managed S3, keys remain with your KMS unless you request Redwood to manage the export process.
- Timeline (typical): snapshot creation: 1 business day; manifest issuance: 1 business day after snapshot verification; tombstone/archive: next 3 business days; overwrite / cryptographic destruction + final verification: up to 10 business days after tombstone (dependent on retention and replication windows). We can compress timelines for an emergency decommission with a committed SLO in an SLA amendment.

What we are attaching to this thread:
- redwood-handback-checklist-v1.xlsx — checkboxes we deliver on handback (manifest, audit logs, snapshots, notarization options).
- snapshot-manifest-20260918.txt — sanitized example manifest (hashes redacted for thread).

Operational notes / rollback:
- Short-term rollback is supported if Lumina elects to escrow the exported snapshot with Redwood for a limited hold period (we typically offer 30 days escrow, extendable by agreement). While escrowed, we maintain a write-once copy and will not purge until the escrow expires or you authorize final deletion. A restore from escrow is a documented operation requiring: Lumina request, two Redwood approvers (security + ops), and a signed consumer attestation describing the purpose.
- If you do NOT escrow and request final handback+purge, we perform tombstone + target overwrite; underlying blocks are scrubbed on the host and we rotate any keys tied to the tenant data. Rehydration is not available after final cryptographic destruction.
- Audit evidence: we provide append-only audit logs (CloudTrail-equivalent), snapshots of KV-store manifests, and a deletion certificate containing the sequence of actions.

Legal / compliance options:
- We can provide a one-time notarized attestation (third-party) or include an on-going monthly attestation service. Pricing and timelines differ.

Next steps suggested:
1) Confirm whether Lumina wants customer-managed export (recommended if you control keys).
2) Decide escrow window (default 30 days) and whether you need notarization.
3) We’ll draft the SLA amendment language to lock in the timeline and SLO.

I’ve copied Karthik (product) and Ben (ops) for technical/operational clarifications.

—
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Irene — thanks, that’s helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from our legal/security teams: 

1) For the notarized attestation, who is the third-party you use (name + jurisdiction)? Our compliance team needs to validate the notary is recognized in our roster.
2) Is the escrowed snapshot stored encrypted with Lumina-managed keys, or Redwood-managed keys? We need to confirm that even during escrow, Lumina maintains control over key material if we choose that option.
3) If we pick escrow + 30-day window and then request a restore for an audit, what are the typical SLA commitments for the restore operation (max time to rehydrate, time to hand over logs)?

Would you prefer Lumina sign the amendment with these options selected, or agree in principle and then finalize the exact key-management language?

Alex
Director, IT Security
Lumina Diagnostics

Subject: Re: Tenant handback: certification & rollback scenarios

Alex — great questions. Quick operational answers below; legal can pick the contract language and we’ll slot the notary name once procurement confirms availability.

1) Notary: we commonly use Harbor Compliance LLC (US, Delaware) for notarized fry-attestations; alternative vendors in EU/APAC are available if necessary. We will confirm the final vendor in the amendment.

2) Escrow encryption: if Lumina chooses escrow with customer-managed keys, we will accept a customer-provided KMS role and encrypt the escrow snapshot with keys you control. If you prefer Redwood-managed escrow, we’ll document key custody and rotate keys post-delete. We can include key custody language in Section 3.2 of the amendment — sample wording attached in the SLA draft.

3) Restore SLA from escrow: standard target is 8 business hours to initiate restore and 48 business hours to fully rehydrate and hand over a validated snapshot for typical dataset sizes (under 5TB). We’ll commit to a longer SLA (expedited) if needed — negotiable in SLA amendment.

Next steps I propose:
- Irene / Karthik: I’ll need a short paragraph confirming the notarization vendor and the mechanics for customer-managed KMS (you can paste text from our standard clause).
- Alex / Lumina: pick escrow = yes/no and preferred escrow duration (30 / 90 days). If yes, indicate whether you’ll provide KMS role.

I’ve attached a draft SLA amendment (initial-sla-amendment-draft.pdf) and highlighted the key clauses. If we get a greenlight on escrow and notarization vendor, I’ll kick off the DocuSign envelope and loop procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: initial-sla-amendment-draft.pdf
